findings.reason: extending build_path_prefix_filter(alias, prefixes, negated=False) keeps one builder that cannot detach its clause from its binding, which is exactly the failure the original helper was introduced to prevent.
findings.text: §24 says it "uses one negated form beside build_path_prefix_filter": build_path_prefix_filter already returns the clause-and-parameters pair, so a negated sibling is a second thin wrapper over render_path_prefix_clause instead of one builder that takes the polarity, and the plan states no reason the existing builder cannot carry a `negated` flag

findings.reason: without the same guard on the paths-side predicates the run reports pending work it cannot drain, which is the non-terminating-phase defect the code-side node was written to close.
findings.text: §24 names the path claims and the code has-work predicates as the sites that must skip excluded rows, but omits the paths-side phase-liveness predicates: has_pending_work (parallel.py:197) and the five _has_pending_scan/expand/triage/enrich/score_work helpers (parallel.py:265-359) match FacilityPath facility-wide, so a scoped run keeps its paths phases alive on the 7,668 /home rows it can never claim; the §14 code-claims node already treated the code-side has-work predicates as an owner to extend, and §24 does not apply the same census to the paths side

findings.reason: the plan should state that the claim predicate is rendered from ExclusionConfig.path_prefixes and that the remaining exclusion families are deliberately claim-invisible, or route every family through one owner, so the two evaluators cannot drift.
findings.text: §24 adds a Cypher negated-prefix predicate in imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py that is a second implementation of the exclusion decision whose owner is ExclusionConfig.should_exclude, and the plan leaves the owner's other families (directories matched by basename, patterns, archive_extensions, dotfiles, scratch) unhonoured by any claim, so a new entry added to excludes.directories or excludes.patterns silently stops excluding at claim time while still excluding at seed and scan time

findings.reason: the section must account for the added surface in its own text, and folding the negation into build_path_prefix_filter would bring the addition back to zero.
findings.text: the section adds a public clause builder in imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py and new exclusion wiring across the path and code claims with this week's public_definitions budget at 0, and it names no symbol it retires or merges and gives no reason nothing can be

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design concentrates behaviour behind few owners (one prefix renderer, one clause+params builder, one create-only node write, one bounded reset spec) rather than spreading wrappers over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §24 extends the exclusion guard to the claims but not to the paths-phase liveness owner it must travel with, and it forks the exclusion predicate away from its ExclusionConfig owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §24 adds a public clause builder and wires exclusion into the claims without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the two implementable sections name the mechanisms they extend (render_path_prefix_clause and build_path_prefix_filter in imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py, GraphClient.create_nodes in imas_codex/graph/client.py, seed_facility_roots in imas_codex/discovery/paths/frontier.py, ExclusionConfig.should_exclude in imas_codex/config/discovery_config.py), and each citation checks out against the code.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §24 adds a second thin clause builder beside build_path_prefix_filter rather than extending it with a negation.
